items.text: WeedCare, a cannabis sales trial commissioned by the canton's Health Department (Abteilung Sucht) and run by the Basel university psychiatric clinics and University of Basel, sells cannabis to enrolled participants through selected pharmacies in Basel-Stadt. Planned to run from September 2022 to January 2027, with up to 374 participants.

Under the federal pilot-trial rules, only adults who live in this canton and can show they already use cannabis may enrol. Participants may use the products only themselves: no passing them on and no use in publicly accessible places. Visitors from outside the canton can't enrol or buy, and the national cannabis ban applies to everyone outside the trials. Each trial is limited to five years, with one extension of up to two years possible; the legal basis for the trials ends on 14 May 2031.
Federal-approved cannabis pilot trial here: WeedCare: regulated sale in pharmacies. Pilot trials are scientific studies approved by the federal health office; organisers report to it yearly.

laws.rule: Basel-Stadt's rest-day and shop-hours Act (Gesetz über öffentliche Ruhetage und Ladenöffnung, §§ 2 to 5): public rest days are the high holidays (Good Friday, Easter Sunday, Whit Sunday and Christmas Day), the other holidays (New Year's Day, Easter Monday, 1 May, Ascension, Whit Monday, St Stephen's Day, the Federal Day of Prayer, and 1 August), and the remaining Sundays. On public rest days, activities that undermine the purpose of the Act or that cause excessive noise or disturbance are banned. Shops may stay open on weekdays from 06:00 to 20:00, on Saturdays and on days before a holiday from 06:00 to 18:00, and on Christmas Eve and Maundy Thursday from 06:00 to 17:00. Among the rest-day exceptions, bakeries, florists and kiosks may open 08:00 to 17:00, and events and businesses for health, recreation, sport, culture or entertainment may run 10:00 to 24:00, but on high holidays only if they do not disturb the special holiday quiet for neighbours or the wider area. Two Advent Sundays a year, shops may open 13:00 to 18:00 without a permit (§ 4a).

laws.rule: The cantonal contraventions Act (Übertretungsstrafgesetz, §§ 5 and 9): after an official warning, causing noise on rest days or during night quiet (23:00 to 07:00), using loudspeakers in public without a permit on rest days or from 22:00 to 07:00, or otherwise making noise beyond what is usually tolerated, is a fine. Begging in an organised way, sending others to beg, or using deceptive methods is a fine. So is begging in public that disturbs public safety, quiet and order, including aggressive begging and begging within five metres of station entrances, public-transport stops and landing stages, cash and ticket machines, shop, bank, post, museum, theatre, cinema, residential, office and public-building entrances, hotels and restaurant terraces, markets and stalls, and in public parks, gardens, cemeteries, playgrounds, school grounds and underpasses. A separate 2024 ordinance (Bettelverordnung, § 1) sets the enforcement steps for § 9(2)(b) to (g): a first offence is recorded and the person is moved on; a repeat brings an official warning and a threat of a fine; a third offence is the listed fixed penalty in item 05.4 of the cantonal fixed-penalty catalogue (the amount itself is in that catalogue, which was not read for this record).
